EMP blasts (directional EMPs aren't really a thing without a really big faraday cage) can't be used within populated areas due to health risks (pacemakers, filtration machines, ect.) and signal jammers are against FCC regulations and carry a heavy fine (in the US at least, there are similar laws in other countries with wireless internet). Wait, so you can kill pacemakers with an EMP? How hard would it be to make handheld emp gun thing?

Very hard. You'd need something the size of a minigun to have enough range to get across the street and it would be one shot and then a massive recharge time, that could fail to charge depending on your weapons construction.

It's basically the same problems as with building a coil gun. You need a decent source to charge the capacitors. If you're able to plug it in to the mains you can drastically decrease the size and charge time, but you lose the portability.

You'd need military-class tech in order to do so, and I'm not even sure it'd be possible, then. I've seen homebrew plans for a one-shot EMP device (initiation burns out the electronics, so it's a one-off), but even those were the size of a couple of ammo cans together.

If you're looking for a "weapon" styled device to kill pacemakers, you'd be better off gutting a microwave oven, and using the magnetron to form a type of directed-energy "Raygun" type of setup, which would still require either external power or a backpack-carried battery-system to power it. Because quadcopters have become very mainstream and popular, and have come with a whole new wave of misinformation. I mean, just look at how people refer to them. "Drones" is supposed to only refer to autonomous or at least semi-autonomous vehicles. That basically means for something to be considered a drone, it has to be capable of performing some level of action without human intervention, which does not apply to any of the things people are flying right now. But because the word is nice and scary and already has terrible connotations from all the controversy about the US using drones to bomb civilians like a bunch of cowards, the word stuck and it's being used against the people who participate in the hobby.

There's a few other reasons:

  1. Jealousy . Quadcopters are pretty neat, they're also expensive. Some people just can't stand to see other people with nice things.

  2. Ignorance. People fear what they don't understand and a lot of people don't know the first thing about quadcopters.

  3. Annoyance. Some quad pilots are obnoxious and know full well when they're crossing the line of what is socially acceptable. Quads are super loud even when they're not flying way too close to you, and some pilots have no consideration for how that makes people feel. Some people are also vehemently against allowing anyone to take their picture/video without their express permission regardless of their public status or the laws surrounding it. Tie all that together and you've got a flying rage generator.
